title: The World’s Largest Penguin Colony Suffers Catastrophic Loss - Nautilus
gist: A study in Cell found chinstrap penguins on Zavodovski Island, once home to the world's largest penguin colony, fell from over 500,000 in 2011 to about 200,000 by 2025, while macaroni penguins rose almost 30 percent.

insights.claim: Chinstrap penguin numbers on Zavodovski Island, site of the world's largest penguin colony, plummeted from more than 500,000 in 2011 to about 200,000 by 2025.
insights.speaker: Devin Reese
insights.so_what: A roughly 60 percent decline in 15 years is a concrete signal of Antarctic ecosystem stress.

insights.claim: Populations were estimated using drone surveys, aerial photos and satellite images detecting patches of penguin poop, by biologists from the U.K., U.S., Germany, South Africa and Chile.
insights.speaker: Devin Reese
insights.so_what: Remote-sensing methods make large-scale wildlife monitoring feasible and repeatable.

insights.claim: Macaroni penguins on the same island grew almost 30 percent, from an estimated 90,000 to more than 200,000, even as chinstraps collapsed.
insights.speaker: Devin Reese
insights.so_what: Shows species-specific divergence under the same environmental conditions, not uniform decline.
